data.rationale: Tile the outer i-dimension by 32 to create 512/32=16 outer tiles. This exposes parallelism across the 30 SMs on Ampere; each tile maps to a CUDA thread block, giving ~16 blocks along i that can be spread across SMs.

Tile j by 128 to create inner tiles of 128 elements. This aligns with 128-byte cache lines (32 fp32 elements) × 4 = 128-element vector chunks, enabling coalesced 128-bit LDG.128 loads. Each tile fits nicely in registers without spilling on Ampere's 65536-register file.

Map the tiled i outer loop to threadblock.x so each block of 32 rows is processed by a distinct CUDA block. With 512/32=16 tiles along i and 512/128=4 tiles along j, we get 16×4=64 blocks — more than enough to saturate 30 SMs with 2 waves.

Map the j tile loop to warps within each block. Each 128-element j-tile is handled by warps in lockstep — with 128/32=4 warps per block, this gives 4×32=128 threads per block doing coalesced 32-element (128-byte) warp-level memory transactions.

Vectorize the j inner loop with width 4 (float4 = 128 bits). This uses LDG.128 instructions, the widest load unit on Ampere, halving the number of memory transactions and improving L2/DRAM throughput utilization for this BW-bound elementwise op.
